lit: to greatly lose what one had hoped for

use.how: Predicate, often after 让人 / 令人: 结果令人大失所望。 Said when something falls far short of what one expected. Already intensified, so no 很 before it.

near.diff: 心灰意冷 is losing heart and the will to go on; 大失所望 is only the letdown when a result is far below expectations.

cue: You queued two hours for a famous restaurant and the food turned out bland and overpriced. How did it leave you?

ctx.s: 这家餐厅名气很大，可菜的味道让我们{大失所望}。
ctx.en: This restaurant is very famous, but the food left us thoroughly disappointed.

ctx.s: 球迷们本来很期待这场比赛，结果主队踢得这么差，大家都{大失所望}。
ctx.en: The fans had been looking forward to the match, but the home team played so badly that everyone was bitterly disappointed.

ctx.s: “新手机怎么样？”“别提了，电池太不耐用，真让人{大失所望}。”
ctx.en: "How's the new phone?" "Don't ask. The battery dies so fast, it's a real letdown."

ctx.s: 他满怀希望地去面试，却{大失所望}地回来了。
ctx.en: He went to the interview full of hope and came back sorely disappointed.

ctx.s: 这部续集剧情拖沓，令不少原著粉丝{大失所望}。
ctx.en: The sequel's plot drags, which badly disappointed many fans of the original book.

ctx.s: 公司公布的业绩远低于预期，投资者{大失所望}，股价随即下跌。
ctx.en: The company's results came in far below expectations; investors were deeply disappointed and the share price fell at once.

bad.s: 爷爷去世了，全家人都{大失所望}。
bad.en: (meant: the whole family was grief-stricken when Grandpa died)
bad.why: It describes a letdown when expectations are not met, not grief over a death or loss.

bad.s: 他对这次考试的结果很{大失所望}。
bad.en: (meant: he was very disappointed with his exam result)
bad.why: The idiom already contains 'greatly', so it cannot take a degree adverb such as 'very' before it.

mean: with many people pitching in at once
lit: seven hands and eight feet: many hands and feet all moving at once

use.how: Adverbial, usually with 地 before a verb: 大家七手八脚地把他扶起来。 Describes a group all helping at the same time, often a bit hurriedly.

near.diff: 手忙脚乱 is one person (or group) flustered and disorganised; 七手八脚 is many people pitching in together.

cue: An old man slips on the pavement and several passers-by rush over at once to lift him up. How do they help him?

ctx.s: 他摔倒了，大家{七手八脚}地把他扶了起来。
ctx.en: He fell over, and everyone rushed in together to help him up.

ctx.s: 搬家那天，朋友们{七手八脚}，一个小时就把东西都搬上了车。
ctx.en: On moving day my friends all pitched in, and within an hour everything was loaded onto the van.

ctx.s: 客人快到了，全家人{七手八脚}地摆桌子、端菜。
ctx.en: The guests were almost here, and the whole family bustled about together setting the table and bringing out dishes.

ctx.s: 车陷进了泥里，路过的村民{七手八脚}地帮忙往外推。
ctx.en: The car got stuck in the mud, and villagers passing by all crowded round to help push it out.

ctx.s: “别急，大家一起来！”同学们{七手八脚}地把倒下的展板重新立了起来。
ctx.en: "Don't panic, everyone together!" The classmates all grabbed hold and set the fallen display board upright again.

ctx.s: 火刚冒烟，邻居们就{七手八脚}地提水来灭，总算没酿成大祸。
ctx.en: As soon as smoke appeared, the neighbours all ran over with buckets of water, and a disaster was narrowly avoided.

bad.s: 他一个人在厨房里{七手八脚}地做饭。
bad.en: (meant: alone in the kitchen, he was cooking in a fluster)
bad.why: It needs many people working at once; one person alone in a flap cannot be described this way.

bad.s: 她做事{七手八脚}，又快又细致。
bad.en: (meant: she is dexterous, quick and careful)
bad.why: It does not praise skill; it pictures a crowd of people all pitching in, often a little chaotically.

use.how: Attributive or predicate for life, activities, content or culture: 丰富多彩的课外活动、生活丰富多彩。 Warmly positive; very common in writing.

near.diff: 五彩缤纷 describes many bright colours you can see; 丰富多彩 describes the variety of life, activities or content.

cue: A brochure wants to praise a school's after-class programme: calligraphy, basketball, choir, robotics and more. What word does it use for the programme?

ctx.s: 学校的课外活动{丰富多彩}，有书法、篮球和合唱。
ctx.en: The school's extracurricular activities are rich and varied: calligraphy, basketball and choir.

ctx.s: 退休以后，奶奶的生活反而更加{丰富多彩}了。
ctx.en: Since retiring, Grandma's life has actually become fuller and more varied.

ctx.s: 这座城市每年夏天都会举办{丰富多彩}的音乐节和夜市。
ctx.en: Every summer the city holds all kinds of lively music festivals and night markets.

ctx.s: “你们春节一般怎么过？”“挺{丰富多彩}的，逛庙会、看灯会、走亲戚。”
ctx.en: "How do you usually spend Spring Festival?" "There's lots going on: temple fairs, lantern shows, visiting relatives."

ctx.s: 这本杂志内容{丰富多彩}，从科技到美食都有涉及。
ctx.en: The magazine's content is wide-ranging, covering everything from technology to food.

ctx.s: 博物馆通过{丰富多彩}的展品，向游客展示了这个民族的历史与文化。
ctx.en: Through a rich variety of exhibits, the museum presents the history and culture of this people to visitors.

bad.s: 她的裙子是红色的，非常{丰富多彩}。
bad.en: (meant: her red dress is very colourful)
bad.why: A single-coloured object is not varied; the idiom praises the variety of life, activities or content.

bad.s: 他很{丰富多彩}地介绍了学校。
bad.en: (meant: he gave a lively introduction to the school)
bad.why: It describes things like life or programmes, not the manner of doing something; it is not used as an adverb.

lit: with a focused heart and a committed will

story.text: Mencius tells of Yi Qiu, the finest go player in the land, who taught two pupils. One gave his whole heart and will to the lesson and listened only to Yi Qiu. The other listened too, but his mind was on a swan that might be about to fly over, and on drawing his bow to shoot it. He learned far less, and Mencius says it was not because he was less clever.

use.how: Usually adverbial with 地: 专心致志地学习、研究、工作。 Also a predicate. Praises sustained, undivided attention to one piece of work.

near.diff: 全神贯注 is total attention in the moment (watching, listening); 专心致志 stresses devoting oneself to a task, often over time.

cue: A scientist turns down every other post and spends years doing nothing but her one research project. How does she work?

ctx.s: 做事要{专心致志}，不能三心二意。
ctx.en: Whatever you do, give it your whole mind; don't keep changing your focus.

ctx.s: 他{专心致志}地研究了十年，终于写成了这本书。
ctx.en: He devoted ten years single-mindedly to his research and finally finished the book.

ctx.s: 这几年她{专心致志}地搞科研，连周末都很少休息。
ctx.en: For the past few years she has devoted herself wholly to research, rarely taking even a weekend off.

ctx.s: “你能不能放下手机？做作业要{专心致志}！”妈妈说。
ctx.en: "Can you put your phone down? Homework needs your full attention!" said Mum.

ctx.s: 要想学好一门乐器，就得{专心致志}，不能今天学这个明天学那个。
ctx.en: To learn an instrument well you have to commit to it, not try one thing today and another tomorrow.

ctx.s: 他辞去了其他职务，好{专心致志}地写完这部小说。
ctx.en: He gave up his other posts so that he could devote himself entirely to finishing the novel.

bad.s: 他{专心致志}地一边看电视一边写作业。
bad.en: (meant: he did his homework while watching TV)
bad.why: It means undivided attention to one task, so doing two things at once contradicts it.

bad.s: 他对女朋友非常{专心致志}。
bad.en: (meant: he is very faithful to his girlfriend)
bad.why: It is about concentrating on work or study, not faithfulness in a relationship.

mean: to treat everyone equally, without favour
lit: to look on all alike and show the same kindness to all

story.text: The phrase goes back to the Tang writer Han Yu. In his essay On Man he wrote that the sage looks on all alike and extends the same benevolence to all, caring for those close at hand while also raising up those far away.

use.how: Predicate, often 对……一视同仁. Said of a teacher, parent, shop, official or law that treats everyone the same, with no favourites.

near.diff: 大公无私 is selflessly putting the public good above one's own interest; 一视同仁 is treating everyone the same.

cue: A teacher gives the same attention and the same marks standard to the top student and the class troublemaker alike. How does she treat them?

ctx.s: 王老师对每个学生都{一视同仁}，从不偏心。
ctx.en: Ms Wang treats every student the same and never plays favourites.

ctx.s: 不管是老顾客还是新顾客，我们店都{一视同仁}。
ctx.en: Regular customer or new one, our shop treats everyone alike.

ctx.s: 法律面前人人平等，执法必须{一视同仁}。
ctx.en: Everyone is equal before the law, so it must be enforced the same way for all.

ctx.s: “凭什么他迟到不扣钱？”“放心，公司的规定对谁都{一视同仁}。”
ctx.en: "Why doesn't he get docked for being late?" "Don't worry, the company's rules apply to everyone equally."

ctx.s: 这家医院对本地病人和外地病人{一视同仁}，挂号排队都一样。
ctx.en: This hospital treats local and out-of-town patients alike; everyone registers and queues the same way.

ctx.s: 父母应该对几个孩子{一视同仁}，否则容易引起兄弟姐妹之间的矛盾。
ctx.en: Parents should treat all their children equally, or it can easily cause friction between siblings.

bad.s: 这两件衣服颜色{一视同仁}，我分不清。
bad.en: (meant: the two shirts are the same colour, I can't tell them apart)
bad.why: It is about treating people without favour, not about things looking identical.

bad.s: 经理对自己的亲戚特别{一视同仁}，总给他们升职。
bad.en: (meant: the manager favours his relatives and keeps promoting them)
bad.why: It means the opposite of favouritism, and it cannot take a degree adverb like 'especially'.

mean: done in one smooth go, without a break

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 这篇文章一气呵成。 Praises writing, a performance or a piece of work done in one uninterrupted, flowing effort.

near.diff: 一蹴而就 is achieving something in one easy step, mostly in negatives (不可能一蹴而就); 一气呵成 praises work done in one unbroken flow.

cue: A writer sits down at midnight and writes a whole short story straight through by dawn, never stopping. How was the story written?

ctx.s: 这篇作文他{一气呵成}，中间一次都没停笔。
ctx.en: He wrote the whole essay in one go, without putting his pen down once.

ctx.s: 她的演奏{一气呵成}，台下掌声雷动。
ctx.en: Her performance flowed from start to finish without a break, and the audience burst into thunderous applause.

ctx.s: 这部电影节奏紧凑，故事讲得{一气呵成}。
ctx.en: The film is tightly paced and tells its story in one seamless sweep.

ctx.s: 灵感来了，他熬了一个通宵，把整首歌{一气呵成}地写完了。
ctx.en: Inspiration struck, and he stayed up all night writing the whole song in one go.

ctx.s: “这幅字写得真流畅！”“是啊，看得出是{一气呵成}的。”
ctx.en: "This calligraphy flows beautifully!" "Yes, you can tell it was written in a single unbroken go."

ctx.s: 装修工人从拆旧到铺地板{一气呵成}，三天就完工了。
ctx.en: The builders went straight from stripping out the old fittings to laying the floor without a pause, and finished in three days.

bad.s: 学好汉语不可能{一气呵成}，要慢慢来。
bad.en: (meant: you can't master Chinese overnight; take it slowly)
bad.why: It praises a piece of work done in one flowing go; it cannot mean that a long-term goal is reached in one step.

bad.s: 这个项目我们断断续续做了三年，终于{一气呵成}。
bad.en: (meant: after three years of stop-start work, we finally finished)
bad.why: It means done without a break, which contradicts three years of stop-start work.

mean: to solve something once and for all

story.text: In the Eastern Han, after the general Dou Xian defeated the Xiongnu, the historian Ban Gu wrote an inscription carved on Mount Yanran to mark the victory. It says that this was a case of toiling once to rest for long, of spending for a short while to gain lasting peace.

use.how: Adverbial (一劳永逸地解决) or attributive (一劳永逸的办法); very often negated: 没有一劳永逸的办法。 Said of a fix that settles a problem for good.

near.diff: 一蹴而就 is about reaching a goal quickly in one step; 一劳永逸 is about one effort whose result lasts and needs no repeating.

cue: Instead of patching the leaking pipe every month, you replace the whole section so it never needs fixing again. What kind of fix is that?

ctx.s: 换根好一点的水管，就能{一劳永逸}，不用每个月都修了。
ctx.en: Put in a better pipe and the problem's solved for good; no more repairs every month.

ctx.s: 学习语言没有{一劳永逸}的办法，必须天天练习。
ctx.en: There's no once-and-for-all shortcut to learning a language; you have to practise every day.

ctx.s: 他把账单都设成自动还款，{一劳永逸}，再也不怕忘记了。
ctx.en: He set all his bills to pay automatically, which settled it for good; now he never worries about forgetting.

ctx.s: “我们干脆把旧系统全换掉吧？”“换了也不是{一劳永逸}，以后还得维护。”
ctx.en: "Why don't we just replace the whole old system?" "Even then it won't be solved forever; it'll still need maintenance."

ctx.s: 健康不是{一劳永逸}的事，锻炼一阵子就停是没用的。
ctx.en: Health isn't something you sort out once and for all; exercising for a while and then stopping is no use.

ctx.s: 政府希望通过这次改革{一劳永逸}地解决农村用水难的问题。
ctx.en: The government hopes this reform will solve the problem of rural water shortages once and for all.

bad.s: 他很{一劳永逸}，什么活都不想干。
bad.en: (meant: he is lazy and doesn't want to do any work)
bad.why: It does not describe a lazy person; it describes a solution that settles a matter for good.

bad.s: 他每天{一劳永逸}地工作到深夜。
bad.en: (meant: he works tirelessly until late every night)
bad.why: It means one effort with a lasting result, so it cannot describe toiling again every day.

lit: to drop a thousand zhang (thousands of metres) in one fall

story.text: Han Yu wrote a poem on hearing the monk Ying play the qin. He describes the music climbing upward note by note, so high that not another inch can be gained, and then suddenly losing its hold and plunging more than a thousand zhang. The image of the music's fall later came to mean any sudden steep decline.

use.how: Predicate after a subject such as 成绩、生意、销量、地位、人气: 生意一落千丈。 Describes a sudden, steep fall in level or standing.

near.diff: 一败涂地 is a complete, crushing defeat; 一落千丈 is a sharp fall in level, such as grades, sales or status.

cue: A popular bakery is caught using expired ingredients, and within a month hardly anyone buys from it. What happened to its business?

ctx.s: 他迷上游戏以后，成绩{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: After he got hooked on video games, his grades took a nosedive.

ctx.s: 那家店被曝光用过期食材，生意{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: Once it came out that the shop used expired ingredients, its business collapsed.

ctx.s: 这位明星因为一句不当言论，人气{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: Because of one inappropriate remark, the star's popularity plummeted.

ctx.s: 自从新的竞争对手进入市场，这个品牌的销量就{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: Ever since a new competitor entered the market, the brand's sales have plunged.

ctx.s: 受伤之后，他的状态{一落千丈}，再也没能回到国家队。
ctx.en: After the injury his form fell away sharply, and he never made it back to the national team.

ctx.s: 随着工厂纷纷倒闭，这座曾经的工业重镇地位{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: As its factories closed one after another, this former industrial hub fell sharply in standing.

bad.s: 他从楼梯上{一落千丈}，摔伤了腿。
bad.en: (meant: he fell down the stairs and hurt his leg)
bad.why: It is figurative, for a sharp fall in level or standing, not a physical fall.

bad.s: 经过努力，他的成绩{一落千丈}，老师很高兴。
bad.en: (meant: through hard work his grades shot up and the teacher was pleased)
bad.why: It means a steep drop, never a rise, so it cannot describe grades improving.

mean: to amaze everyone with a sudden first success
lit: with one cry, it astonishes everyone

story.text: King Wei of Qi spent his days drinking and left the state to drift. Chunyu Kun, who liked riddles, asked him about a great bird in the palace that for three years had neither flown nor sung. The king answered that this bird, once it flew, would soar to the sky, and once it sang, would astonish everyone. He then took the government in hand.

use.how: Predicate: 他在比赛中一鸣惊人。 Said of someone unknown or quiet who suddenly does something remarkable, often a first work or first big contest.

near.diff: 一举成名 just means becoming famous at a stroke; 一鸣惊人 stresses that someone overlooked suddenly astonishes everyone.

cue: A shy student nobody noticed enters the speech contest for the first time and wins first prize, stunning the whole school. What did he do?

ctx.s: 这个平时不爱说话的同学，在演讲比赛中{一鸣惊人}，拿了第一名。
ctx.en: This usually quiet student stunned everyone in the speech contest and took first place.

ctx.s: 她的第一部小说就{一鸣惊人}，卖了上百万册。
ctx.en: Her very first novel was a sensation, selling over a million copies.

ctx.s: 这支没人看好的小球队竟然打败了冠军，真是{一鸣惊人}。
ctx.en: This little team that nobody rated actually beat the champions; what a stunning breakthrough.

ctx.s: “你准备了这么久，有把握吗？”“不试试怎么知道？说不定能{一鸣惊人}呢。”
ctx.en: "You've prepared so long; are you confident?" "How will I know if I don't try? Maybe I'll surprise everyone."

ctx.s: 他默默练了三年，决心在全国比赛上{一鸣惊人}。
ctx.en: He trained quietly for three years, determined to astonish everyone at the national championship.

ctx.s: 这家初创公司推出的第一款产品就{一鸣惊人}，迅速占领了市场。
ctx.en: The start-up's very first product made a huge splash and quickly captured the market.

bad.s: 他突然大叫，{一鸣惊人}，吓了我一跳。
bad.en: (meant: he suddenly shouted and startled me)
bad.why: It is figurative, for a sudden remarkable success, not a loud noise that startles someone.

bad.s: 他是多年的老冠军，这次又{一鸣惊人}地赢了。
bad.en: (meant: the long-time champion won again this time)
bad.why: It implies a sudden success after obscurity, which does not fit an established champion winning again.

use.how: Noun phrase, the object of 助 (also 出 or 尽): 助你一臂之力、为……出一臂之力。 Offering or asking for a specific piece of help; a little formal and polite.

near.diff: 助人为乐 describes someone who enjoys helping others as a trait; 一臂之力 is the help given in one particular case.

cue: Your friend is short of people to run a charity event, and you politely offer to help out. What do you offer them?

ctx.s: 你要是搬家缺人手，我可以助你{一臂之力}。
ctx.en: If you're short of hands for the move, I can give you a hand.

ctx.s: “这次活动缺一个翻译，你能不能助我们{一臂之力}？”
ctx.en: "We're short of an interpreter for this event. Could you lend us a hand?"

ctx.s: 多亏老同学助了我{一臂之力}，我才渡过了难关。
ctx.en: It was only thanks to an old classmate's help that I got through that difficult time.

ctx.s: 洪水过后，各地志愿者纷纷赶来，助灾区{一臂之力}。
ctx.en: After the flood, volunteers poured in from all over to help the stricken area.

ctx.s: 如贵公司有需要，我方愿助{一臂之力}。
ctx.en: Should your company need it, we would be glad to lend our assistance.

ctx.s: 这项新技术为医生早期发现疾病助了{一臂之力}。
ctx.en: This new technology has given doctors a helping hand in detecting disease early.

bad.s: 他{一臂之力}地帮我搬了箱子。
bad.en: (meant: he helped me carry the boxes)
bad.why: It is a noun phrase used as the object of a verb meaning 'help', not an adverb before a verb.

bad.s: 我只有{一臂之力}，搬不动这么重的箱子。
bad.en: (meant: I'm not strong enough to lift such a heavy box)
bad.why: It means help given to someone, not a measure of one's own physical strength.
